sections.name: File setup, GeometryValidationError, isPosition, equalPosition
sections.title: Imports, size limit and basic helpers
sections.what: Brings in the area library and shape types, sets the size limit at 100,000, defines the validation error type, and provides helpers that check a position is two finite numbers and that two positions are equal.
sections.why: Gives the validators their building blocks and a fixed limit.
sections.watch_out: The limit is a fixed value and is not configurable from outside.

sections.name: validateRing
sections.title: Ring check
sections.what: Checks that a ring has at least four points, that each point is a valid longitude and latitude within range, and that the first and last points are the same.
sections.why: Makes sure each outline is a closed, mappable shape before it is used.
sections.watch_out: It does not check whether the outline crosses itself, so a bow-tie shape would pass.

sections.name: validatePolygon
sections.title: Polygon check
sections.what: Checks that a polygon has at least one ring and checks each ring.
sections.why: A polygon is only valid when all its rings are valid.

sections.name: validateParcelGeoJson
sections.title: Overall shape check
sections.what: Checks the size of the serialized input, that it is an object, and that its type is Polygon or MultiPolygon. Returns a clean copy with only the type and coordinates, dropping any other fields.
sections.why: Single entry point that makes sure stored shapes are clean and of allowed types.
sections.watch_out: Extra fields such as names are silently removed, so they never reach storage through this path.

sections.name: GeospatialService, geospatialService
sections.title: Geospatial service and area calculation
sections.what: Provides a validation method and an area calculation that validates the shape, measures its square metres with Turf, rejects zero or invalid areas, and returns hectares and acres from the same figure.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the app one trusted source for land area.
sections.watch_out: The acre conversion uses a fixed constant, so areas match the international acre only.

summary: Checks that land shape data is a valid, closed, bounded GeoJSON polygon or multi-polygon, and calculates its area in square metres, hectares and acres.
purpose: Makes sure only usable shapes are stored and that area figures come from the stored shape rather than typed-in numbers.
why: Likely reason: area figures are shown to users, so they must come from validated geometry. Reason for the size limit is not stated in the code.
how: It first checks the size of the serialized shape, then checks it is an object of a supported type, then checks each ring's points and closure. It rebuilds a clean copy with only type and coordinates. For area, it validates the shape, measures it with the Turf library, rejects zero areas, and converts to hectares and acres.
inputs: A parcel shape as a plain object in GeoJSON form.
outputs: A cleaned shape, or an error explaining what is wrong, and an area result with its source marked as calculated from geometry.
risks: The size limit counts characters of the text rather than bytes, despite the name. The ring check does not detect self-crossing outlines. Extra fields in the input are silently dropped.
debug: If a shape is rejected, read the error message, which states the failed rule. If areas look wrong, check that coordinates are longitude then latitude and that the shape is closed.
